'''Stanley Jerome Farlow''' (born 1937) is an American  [[mathematician]] specializing in [[differential equation]]s. For many years he has been a professor at the [[University of Maine]].

== Life ==
Farlow earned a bachelor's degree in physics at [[Iowa State University]] and a master's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Iowa]].<ref name="umaine.edu">{{cite web|url=http://math.umaine.edu/~farlow/index.htm|title=Home page|publisher=University of Maine Mathematics Department|accessdate=2 May 2018}}</ref>
From 1962 to 1968 he was a lieutenant commander in the PHS, completing his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics at [[Oregon State University]] in 1967. His doctoral supervisor was Ronald Bernard Guenther, and his doctoral dissertation was on ''Existence Theorems for Periodic Solutions of Parabolic Partial Differential Equations''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=91890}}</ref>

He is currently a Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at the [[University of Maine]].<ref name="umaine.edu"/>

== Books ==
Farlow is the author of several books in mathematics, including
*''Partial Differential Equations for Scientists and Engineers'' (Wiley, 1982; Russian translation, Moscow: Mir, 1985; Dover, 1993)<ref>Reviews of ''Partial Differential Equations for Scientists and Engineers'':
*{{cite journal | last=Morgan | first=K. | title=Book review: Partial differential equations for scientists and engineers | journal=International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering | publisher=Wiley | volume=19 | issue=4 | year=1983 | issn=0029-5981 | doi=10.1002/nme.1620190413 | pages=625–625| doi-access=free }}
*{{cite journal | last=Farlow | first=Stanley J. | last2=Becker | first2=Stephen F. | title=Partial Differential Equations for Scientists and Engineers | journal=American Journal of Physics | publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) | volume=53 | issue=7 | year=1985 | issn=0002-9505 | doi=10.1119/1.14292 | pages=702–702}}
*Tweddle, J. Christopher (January 2010), [https://www.maa.org/publications/maa-reviews/partial-differential-equations-for-scientists-and-engineers MAA Reviews]</ref>
*Applied Mathematics for Management, Life Science, and Social Science (with Gary M. Haggard, Random House, 1988)
*''Finite Mathematics and Its Applications'' (with Gary M. Haggard, Random House, 1988; 2nd ed., McGraw Hill, 1994)
*''Introduction to Calculus with Applications'' (with Gary M. Haggard, McGraw Hill, 1990)
*''An Introduction to Differential Equations and Their Applications'' (McGraw Hill, 1994; Dover, 2006)
*Differential Equations and Linear Algebra (with James E. Hall, Jean Marie Mc Dill, and Beverly H. West, Prentice Hall, 2002)
*''Paradoxes in Mathematics'' (Dover, 2014)<ref>Reviews of ''Paradoxes in Mathematics'': 
*''Advanced Mathematics: A Transitional Reference'' (Wiley, 2020)
*Becker, Glenn (October 2014), [https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/paradoxes-in-mathematics MAA Reviews]
*Cobreros, Pablo, {{MR|3243572}}</ref>
*Advanced Mathematics: A Transitional Reference (Wiley, 2020)

He is also the editor of:
*''Self-Organizing Methods in Modeling: GMDH Type Algorithms'' (Marcel Dekker, 1984)
